▪︎lubiprostone: ⇡Cl-rich intestinal secretion via chloride channel receptors (IBS-C after fiber & osmotic laxatives)
, eluxadoline, rifaximin; bile acid sequestrants, alosetron
▪︎loperamide: 1st-line for intermittent or alternating D/C; inhibits peristalsis; ⍉for abd discomfort
▪︎cholestyramine (bile acid sequestrant) 2nd-line for diarrhea: up to 50% w/ functional diarrhea have bile acid malabsorption (⍉absorbed bile acids → colonic secretion & motility)
▪︎⍉response to antispasmodics or comorbid depression → TCAs (amitriptyline, nortriptyline, desipramine)
▪︎antispasmodics = 1st-line for abd discomfort/pain; PRN short-term & in anticipation of known stressors
: older age (>60–65), dehydration, ↓ fiber & physical activity
▪︎chronic: med AEs, IBS, hypothyroidism, CRC, neuro (MS, Parkinson, spinal cord damage), idiopathic w/ slow or normal colonic transit
•stool too hard, too small, too difficult to pass
•straining; sensation of incomplete evacuation or obstruction
(→ CRC or IBD): rectal bleeding, heme(+) stool, IDA, wt loss >10 lb, recent onset w/o obvious explanation, FHx CRC or IBD → further eval incl endoscopy (colonoscopy or flex sig)
functional constipation ≥2 of: <3 BMs/wk, straining, lumpy or hard stools, sensation of incomplete evacuation or obstruction, manual maneuvers to facilitate defecation

Tx once dangerous causes unlikely/ruled out: lifestyle modification & pharm; lifestyle: H2O ≥8 cups/day, fiber 20–35 g/day, exercise regularly, attempt BMs postprandially; educate daily BMs are ⍉necessarily the norm or required for good health
loosen stools & ↑ freq of BMs; classes: bulk-forming, surfactants, osmotic, stimulant
(psyllium, methylcellulose, bran, polycarbophil): absorb H2O & ↑ fecal mass → more freq BMs, softer stool, minimal AEs
: PEG, Mg citrate, lactulose, sorbitol; draw H2O into intestine → ↑ freq & improve consistency
(bisacodyl, senna, sodium picosulfate): alter lyte transp across intestinal mucosa & ↑ intestinal motor activity; caution long-term (risk K & Na depletion)
(docusate): lowers surface tension of stool; generally less effective than other constipation meds
▪︎chart also: saline preps (Mg hydroxide, Mg sulfate), lubricants (mineral oil), prokinetics (tegaserod, metoclopramide)

failing lifestyle & laxatives: suppositories, enemas (tap H2O, soapsuds, mineral oil, sodium phosphate), secretory agents (linaclotide, lubiprostone, plecanatide), manual fecal disimpaction; glycerin & bisacodyl suppositories liquefy stool
▪︎fecal impaction (solid immobile stool in rectum): sometimes manual fragmentation then mineral oil enemas

: most serious AE of sodium phosphate enemas in older adults → severe life-threatening lyte & fluid derangements: extreme hyperphosphatemia w/ reciprocal hypocalcemia, AKI & acute phosphate nephropathy, volume depletion → cardiac dysrhythmias, sz, death
